text: I came here to support you. I have been living in Israel for 9 years and my hebrew is far from fluent. I dont really read. Not sure how exactly this happened, but honestly, we have 3 kids, I am part of minimum 3 WhatsApp groups for each kids school, for each chug there is whatsapp group… it takes eternity for me to even try to read what people write where and filtrate important/non important things… so I switchced to automated translation to be able to read at least part of the messages what people write there with lethal frequency (and I am anyway not able to keep up 🤣). Hebrew verbal communication is done on daily basis, but it is quite same topics, so while I master shopping in Hebrew, in the doctor I am quite speechless, same as in other not super regular occasion (pub, misrad hapnim, often at work…). I have never took ulpan (simply because with babies one cant attend intensive course lasting for several months and now with the work plus still small independent children it is even more impossible). So this is probably with what I am going to stay at least for next few years 🙂. While it is amazing you want to work on yourself, be also nice on you. You work with what you have got and language learning pace is really not possible to generalize. People have variable skills, but also not everyone has same environment and good conditions to learn, or sometimes you are overwhelmed by everyone speaking foreign language and then in your free time you dont want to be again stuck in learning that language, but you want to spend time with your native language to keep your mental health stable and it is ok. So dont shame yourself for not know hebrew good enough compared to the time you have been here, dont feel guilty for that. Nobody who doesn’t walk in your shoes has right to judge you ❤️.
